title: Diwali Puja Outfit Ideas for Women: What to Wear for Lakshmi Puja
excerpt: What to wear for Lakshmi puja at home on Diwali: graceful kurta sets, easy fabrics and colours that feel festive, whether you are in India or abroad.
body:
For Lakshmi puja at home, the best outfit is a soft, well-fitted kurta set with a dupatta: traditional enough for the aarti, comfortable enough to sit on the floor, and pretty enough for every family photo that follows. Think light colours, breathable fabric and a dupatta you can cover your head with when the moment comes. This year Diwali falls on 8 November 2026, so there is still time to plan a look you will love.

## What makes a good puja outfit

A puja is not a party. You will light diyas, sit cross-legged for a while, move around the kitchen with prasad, and probably bend down to draw or fix the rangoli. So the outfit has to work with your body, not against it.

Look for three things. First, a kurta with enough room at the hip so sitting on the floor feels easy. Second, pants or palazzos rather than a tight churidar if you plan to sit for long. Third, a dupatta that is long and light, because you will drape it over your head during the aarti and you do not want it slipping every few seconds.

Keep the sleeves close to the arm. Wide, floaty sleeves look lovely but are not your friend near an open diya flame.

## Colours that feel right for Lakshmi puja

Many families prefer bright, auspicious shades for Diwali: red, yellow, orange, pink and gold. Others love soft pastels that photograph beautifully under fairy lights. There is no single rule, so follow your family tradition first and your mood second.

| Colour family | Why it works | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| Peach, pink, coral | Warm and cheerful, flatters most skin tones | Daytime and evening puja |
| Off-white with colour embroidery | Fresh and elegant, lets diya light glow | Small, quiet home puja |
| Mint and sage green | Calm, new and fresh | Women who find red too loud |
| Lavender | Soft but still festive | Evening puja with photos |
| Red, maroon, mustard | Classic Diwali shades | Traditional households |

## Fabric matters more than you think

Indoor heating abroad and a room full of lit diyas can make a home surprisingly warm. Cotton and cotton blends are the most comfortable choice for a long puja because they breathe and do not cling. Kota doria and organza dupattas add a festive finish without adding weight.

If you like a cleaner look, the [Off-White Embroidered Cotton Kurta Set](/products/off-white-embroidered-cotton-flex-kurta-pant-organza-dupatta-set/) feels pure and calm, which many women love for a puja. Pair it with gold jhumkas and a red bindi to keep it festive.

## From puja to dinner in one outfit

Most of us do the puja, then sit down to a family meal, then step out to see the neighbourhood lights or a friend's party. Plan one outfit that can shift with you.

A simple trick is to start the puja with your dupatta draped over both shoulders and head, then switch to a one-shoulder drape for dinner. Add statement earrings, swap flat sandals for embellished juttis, and you have a second look in two minutes.

Buying ethnic wear outside India often means guessing sizes, then paying a local tailor to fix it. A puja outfit should sit comfortably when you kneel and bend, so fit really matters here.

## Finishing touches for the puja

- **Jewellery:** gold-tone jhumkas, a few glass bangles and a small maang tikka if you like. Keep the neck light so your dupatta sits well.
- **Footwear:** you will be barefoot for the puja itself, so choose easy slip-on juttis or kolhapuris.
- **Hair:** a low bun or a side braid with a gajra keeps hair away from the diya flame.

For a fresh, light option that still feels special, the [Mint Green Hand Block Print Cotton Kurta Pant Dupatta Set](/products/mint-green-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-dupatta-set-with-hand-work-yoke/) has a hand-worked yoke that catches the diya light nicely.

## Frequently asked questions

**What colour should I wear for Lakshmi puja?**
Red, yellow, pink, peach, orange and gold are traditional favourites. Soft pastels are also widely worn now. Follow your family's custom, and avoid all-black if you are unsure.

**Can I wear a cotton kurta set for Diwali puja?**
Yes. Cotton is one of the best choices because it breathes and is safe and comfortable near diyas. An organza or kota doria dupatta makes it feel festive.

**Should I cover my head during the aarti?**
Many families do, so choose a long, light dupatta that stays in place. It is a personal and family choice.

**How early should I order from abroad for Diwali?**
